newsitem.title: ITALY: Milan shares end firmer following bonds, US stocks.
newsitem.headline: Milan shares end firmer following bonds, US stocks.

text.p: Italian shares closed firmer on Monday helped by the strong rally in domestic bonds and the lira, and reflecting the higher trend to U.S. stocks on Wall Street, dealers said.

The market was also given support by words over the weekend by Treasury Minister Carlo Aveglio Ciampi who said he saw April inflation at 1.9 percent while CPI may stabilise at around 1.5 percent at the end of June. Earlier, March Italian CPI was confirmed at 2.2 percent after February's 2.4 percent.
The blue-chip Mib30 index of leading Italian stocks ended up 2.39 percent at 17,630, while the all-share Mibtel closed 2.13 percent higher at 11,932.
Dealers said the major focus today for the Italian market was Wall Street, which started on a firmer footing led by a rally in U.S. bonds and good demand for high technology stocks.

Leading Italian stocks like energy giant ENI rose 1.96 percent to 8,172 lire while industrial group Fiat firmed 1.98 percent to 5,351 lire, but information technology group Olivetti was one to slip, off 0.16 percent at 611.9 lire.
Dealers said there was little specific news to move individual stocks, with the market largely content to follow events in other financial markets while taking a lead from Wall Street's direction.
